newsitem.title: CANADA: Mountain Province wants to raise stake.
newsitem.headline: Mountain Province wants to raise stake.

text.p: Canadian diamond explorer Mountain Province Mining Inc said on Friday it hopes to increase its half stake in two exploration projects in the Northwest Territories.
Chairman Paul Shatzko said potential suitors would prefer to deal with fewer partners if they decided to back the company's goal of developing a diamond mine.

The company controls 50 percent of the AK/CJ property, about 100 km southeast of Lac de Gras where Dia Met Minerals Ltd is partnered with BHP Minerals Inc to build the first diamond mine in North America.
Its partners are Glenmore Highlands Inc with 40 percent and Camphor Ventures Inc with 10 percent.
"It would be easier to have a 90-10 set-up," Shatzko told Reuters after the company's annual meeting.
"In the next 30-60 days, it would be a good idea to look at that kind of arrangement," he said. Glenmore officials were unavailable for comment on merger prospects.
Shatzko said Mountain Province expects a takeover offer from a major partner next year after bulk sampling is completed at the AK 5034 kimberlite pipe.
He said company's that have shown a preliminary interest include RTZ Corp Plc, De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd and Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd.
"De Beers would be the favored candidate," he said.

After a "highly successful" 100-tonne mini bulk sample was completed earlier this year at the 5034 pipe, a C$20 million bulk sample of between 3,000 and 10,000 tonnes is planned for next spring, company president Jan Vandersande told shareholders.

The bulk sample will attempt to substantiate Mountain Province's current estimates, which say the 5034 pipe contains "at least 20 million tonnes grading 3 carats per tonne" for a total value of between US$1.8 billion and US$3 billion.
In addition, C$4.0 million is slated for exploration outside of the 5034 on the AK and CJ claim blocks. Mountain Province's share of all exploration costs is 50 percent.
Mountain Province's largest declared shareholder is Societe Generale, a Paris-based financial institution with 20.12 percent of the issued shared as of April 25, 1996.
